"1244-01000871-50Z" appears to be silkscreened on the board in the FCC photos. :The device is using two [http://www.rfmw.com/datasheets/skyworks/SE5022T_DS.pdf '''Skyworks''' ('''SiGe''') SE5022T / 5022T 5GHz Power Amplifiers] :and two [http://www.skyworksinc.com/uploads/documents/SKY85601_11_202865A.pdf '''Skyworks''' SKY85601 (SKY85601-11?) SPDT Switch w/ LNA modules]. :The flip-up antenna ('''LYNWAVE''' ALA110-221020) is connected via an internal U.FL / IPEX connector.
Based on '''Edimax''''s provided drivers, the USB ID of the device is presumed to be 7392:a822. :The drivers also indicate a single-stream RTL8811AU based device :(USB ID: 7392:a811, '''AC600''', EW-7811UAC?) may be released later by '''Edimax'''. <small> :Warning: each time the device scans it seems to cause a 3second delay in :packets for several seconds (Linux 3.13 using patched 1.0.1.6 drivers). :As network manager does this by default every 2mins this is can be very problematic. </small> ===Review of Linux Compatibility=== <small>[http://m.linux-hardware-guide.com/2013-11-16-edimax-ew-7822uac-ac1200-wifi-dual-band-usb-3-0 Edimax EW-7822UAC] is a USB WiFi stick, which supports wireless connections 802.11ac. :The adapter bases on the Realtek RTL8812AU chipset and has the USB ID 7392:a822: Bus 003 Device 002: ID 7392:a822 Edimax Technology Co., Ltd Until now no driver for the EW-7822UAC is included in the standard Linux kernel. :However, ''Edimax'' provides a [http://www.edimax.com/images/Image/Driver_Utility/Wireless/NIC/EW-7822UAC/EW-7822UAC_linux_v4.2.2_7502.20130517.tar.gz Linux driver] for this adapter, :which has to be compiled from source per hand.
Alternatively, on can use a Open-Source Linux driver from [https://github.com/abperiasamy/rtl8812AU_8821AU_linux GitHub] :by downloading the ZIP file which is available on the linked page. The downloaded file can be compiled by: cd Downloads/rtl8812AU_8821AU_linux-master make sudo make install sudo modprobe 8812au The compiled kernel module 8812au.ko will be used automatically for the stick after reboot.
As of March 2017, Edimax has provided [https://edimax.freshdesk.com/support/solutions/articles/14000041287-how-to-install-ew-78xx-11ac-adapter-in-linux-with-kernel-higher-than-v4-1 a detailed tutorial] for compiling the Open Source driver on higher kernel versions (e.g. above 4.1) </small>
